title: Fynaptix · AI Biotech Research
heading: AI Biotech Intelligence
subheading: AI-native drug discovery, computational biology & longevity capital
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Biotech carries binary clinical risk; AI-discovery names trade on catalysts, not revenue. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.sub: INTELLIA'S LONVO-Z PDUFA DATE CONFIRMED · HAELO PHASE 3 SHOWED 87% ATTACK-RATE REDUCTION
kpis.label: The FDA set a firm PDUFA date for lonvo-z in hereditary angioedema — the clearest approval timeline yet for what would be the first in-vivo CRISPR therapy ever approved. Intellia also secured a $400M credit facility to fund the eventual launch. Still a decision, not an approval, but the most concrete date on this page

kpis.sub: ILLUMINA (ILMN) OFFICIALLY JOINS THE S&P 500 TODAY · FRESH 52-WEEK HIGH $239.55
kpis.label: First time back since the 2023 GRAIL-spinoff drop; shares are up 143% over the past 12 months on a genuine earnings turnaround (FY2025 net income $850M) and a Sept 9 UBS upgrade to Buy with price target raised to $260 from $135

kpis.sub: TEMPUS AI (TEM) ONE-WEEK STOCK SURGE · 100K-GENOME PLATFORM + $9.5M ARPA-H AWARD
kpis.label: Tempus announced a platform pairing 100,000 disease-specific whole genomes with longitudinal outcomes data (aiming for 1M) and secured ARPA-H funding for an autonomous cardiology AI agent — enough to push its ARKG weight to #2 (9.23%), just behind 10x Genomics. The Guardant litigation overhang hasn't moved

kpis.sub: ARKG AUM SLIPS TO $1.93B EVEN AS THE FUND HITS A FRESH 52-WEEK HIGH
kpis.label: Price closed at $51.64 (52-week high $52.09), yet AUM fell from $2.00B two weeks ago — a sign of redemptions into strength, not new money. Top-10 concentration rose to 60.41% as Tempus's rally dominates the weighting

themes.tag: A DIAGNOSTICS NAME RE-RATES ON A DATA-PLATFORM STORY, NOT A LEGAL WIN
themes.title: Tempus AI surges ~40% in a week on a 100k-genome platform and ARPA-H cardiology funding
themes.description: Tempus announced a platform pairing 100,000 disease-specific whole genomes with longitudinal clinical outcomes (aiming for 1M long-term) and secured up to $9.5M in ARPA-H funding for an autonomous cardiology AI agent. The rally pushed Tempus to ARKG's #2 holding (9.23%, from roughly 8% two weeks ago) — but the Guardant litigation overhang that has dogged the stock all year is completely unchanged. Business momentum and legal risk are running on separate tracks here.

themes.tag: A TOOLING INCUMBENT'S FUNDAMENTALS AND FLOWS ARRIVE TOGETHER
themes.title: Illumina officially rejoins the S&P 500 today, first time since the 2023 GRAIL-spinoff drop
themes.description: The index add follows a genuine fundamental turnaround — FY2025 net income of $850M, a Sept 9 UBS upgrade to Buy with price target raised to $260 (from $135), and seven analysts raising FY26 EPS estimates over the past 60 days. Shares hit a fresh 52-week high of $239.55 on Sept 18, up 143% over the trailing 12 months. Index funds must now hold shares — a mechanical flow tailwind layered on top of an already-improving operating story.

themes.tag: A REAL TECHNICAL MILESTONE IN THE LEAST MATURE LAYER OF THE STACK
themes.title: Quantum-Si demonstrates detection of 18 of 20 amino acids on Proteus, closing in on its 2026 goal
themes.description: Announced Sept 15, this is the clearest sign yet that Quantum-Si's next-gen protein-sequencing platform actually works, even as the commercial Proteus launch remains a confirmed year late (Q2 2027) after August's workforce reduction. An expanded roadshow through Leiden, Paris and London this month, with Barcelona, Rome, Munich and Berlin added for Q4, suggests the company is building commercial momentum ahead of that delayed launch.

themes.tag: THE FIELD'S CLEAREST APPROVAL TIMELINE GETS MORE CONCRETE — AND ONE COMPETING TIMELINE GETS LONGER
themes.title: Intellia's lonvo-z gets a firm PDUFA date (Mar 10, 2027) while Insilico's rentosertib approval math pushes to 2029-2030
themes.description: Intellia's HAELO Phase 3 data showed an 87% reduction in hereditary angioedema attack rates, and the company secured a $400M credit facility to fund launch — the most concrete approval date in AI/gene-editing biotech. Separately, Insilico's own lead investigator now estimates rentosertib is three to four years from Phase III start to approval, pointing to 2029-2030 rather than the 2027-28 window discussed previously. Progress on one front, a longer runway on another — the sector's zero-approvals fact hasn't changed either way.

rows.angle: Isomorphic partnership renewed (~$1.2B+); new Chai Discovery antibody-design collab; $1.7B Relation Therapeutics target deal
rows.watch for: No new catalyst this week; Q2 sales +3% to $14.4B and reaffirmed FY26 guidance remain the operative numbers. Chai Discovery's $400M Series C (July, $3.8B valuation) — backed by Novartis alongside Lilly and Pfizer — is the closest thing to fresh news, underscoring that the multi-partner AI bet (Chai, Orionis, Relation) keeps compounding without needing any single platform to deliver a win

rows.watch for: Lilly co-innovation lab now ~8 months into build-out with no new headline this week; BioNeMo's expanded model set (RNA structure prediction, molecular synthesis, toxicity prediction) continues to widen the compute moat quietly in the background as more pharma platforms plug in

tiers.label: AI-Native Platforms — Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Catalysts here are partnerships, IND filings, and readouts — not revenue.

rows.angle: Millions of automated cell-imaging experiments feeding AI "maps of biology"; collabs with Roche, Bayer, Merck, Sanofi, Genentech
rows.watch for: Shares have rebounded off the 52-week low, up 8.78% (Sept 17) and 4.8% (Sept 18) to close near $3.71, with early data on REC-7735 (an oral, twice-daily drug targeting PIK3CA-H1047R-driven solid tumors) drawing investor interest at the Sept 15 Morgan Stanley Healthcare Conference. The trial is still in dose-finding/dose-expansion, so this looks like sentiment repair rather than a new efficacy signal

rows.angle: Physics-based + ML molecular simulation; software revenue cushions pipeline risk
rows.watch for: Launched Bunsen, an agentic AI co-scientist pairing physics-based simulation with an LLM layer to run molecular-discovery workflows — a genuine platform expansion beyond last week's Tectora spinout ($55M round with NEA & RA Capital). No new clinical data on SGR-1505/SGR-3515 this week

rows.angle: Motion-based protein modeling for precision oncology; zovegalisib advancing
rows.watch for: Presented at the Sept 16 Morgan Stanley Healthcare Conference — its second investor conference in nine days after Wells Fargo on Sept 8 — with no new data disclosed. The ~$463M ATM equity facility remains a live dilution overhang ahead of the early-2027 Dynamo Phase 3 readout for zovegalisib

rows.watch for: Stock remains stabilized post-pullback with no fresh catalyst since the ERS Congress posters concluded Sept 9; shares stay above the $16 IPO price but well off the Aug 25 all-time high of $20.38. GB-0895's global Phase 3 (SOLAIRIA-1/2) is unchanged

rows.angle: Live-cell single-molecule tracking — upsized IPO Feb 4 2026 at $18/sh, $381M raised
rows.watch for: Still no news to resolve the Aug 4 lock-up overhang or the board resignations that preceded the Aug 10 Merck-advisor addition; shares remain well below the $18 IPO price with no near-term catalyst visible

private_watchlist.name: Isomorphic Labs
private_watchlist.note: AlphaFold 3 lineage; Thrive Capital-led round adds MGX, Temasek, CapitalG & UK Sovereign AI Fund alongside Alphabet/GV. Chris Butler, who runs drug discovery at Isomorphic, pushed back this week on suggestions that AI-pacing calls would slow the company down — "we're able to still progress regardless of what decisions are made elsewhere" — and noted its models are "locked down in-house." No update on the delayed ISM8969 trial timeline (still targeting first trials by year-end 2026, a year behind the original 2025 target); being Alphabet-owned makes a near-term IPO unlikely regardless.

private_watchlist.name: Insilico Medicine
private_watchlist.note: Rentosertib's realistic FDA timeline just got clearer and less exciting than the headline suggests: with Phase III (GENESIS-IPF) underway since July 2026, the lead investigator now puts Phase III start to approval at three to four years under favorable conditions — pointing to 2029-2030, not the 2027-28 window previously discussed. Insilico did secure its first FDA Fast Track Designation (July 29) and IND clearance for a rentosertib inhalation formulation, plus a Nature Biotechnology paper suggesting rentosertib may reverse biological aging on proteomic clocks — an interesting longevity-adjacent data point, but the approval math just got longer, not shorter. Still the only name here already public (HKEX, Dec 2025, $292M IPO).

private_watchlist.name: Xaira Therapeutics
private_watchlist.note: Launched X-Cell, its first virtual cell model (4.9B parameters, trained on the 25.6M-cell X-Atlas/Pisces dataset), in March 2026. Built out its clinical leadership over the summer — Ci Chu to Chief Discovery Officer, Bo Wang to Chief AI Scientist, Rachel Lane as SVP Business Development & Operations — continuing the shift from platform-building toward actually running trials, though no trial has started yet. No fresh update this week.

private_watchlist.name: NewLimit
private_watchlist.note: Epigenetic reprogramming for longevity (Founders Fund, Lilly Ventures, Jun 2026); moved its first candidate medicine into large-scale manufacturing in January, still targeting clinical entry as early as 2027. NewLimit alone accounts for roughly 71% of this year's disclosed longevity funding (~$614M through August). Retro Biosciences (Sam Altman-backed) formally announced the initial close of its raise at a $1.8B valuation (May 22) — no longer just "reportedly working to close" — with cumulative funding now over $1.18B. The sector's capital keeps concentrating hard in cellular reprogramming rather than broadening.

bear_case.title: Biology still fails in the clinic — and the AI-drug approval math just got longer
bear_case.description: Zero AI-discovered drugs have reached full FDA approval, out of 200+ now in clinical development. Insilico's own lead investigator now puts rentosertib's realistic timeline at 2029-2030 (three to four years from Phase III start), not the 2027-28 window previously discussed — a reminder that even the field's clearest proof point is still years, not quarters, away.

bear_case.title: Diagnostics litigation remains a three-way mess with no resolution in sight
bear_case.description: No new movement this week on any of the three active fronts: Guardant's suit against Tempus (surviving dismissal since Aug 27), Tempus's dismissed-with-prejudice suit against Guardant (under appeal since Feb), or the $245.2M TwinStrand judgment against Guardant (also under appeal to the Federal Circuit). Three lawsuits, two companies, years of legal spend ahead regardless of outcome.

bear_case.title: Sentiment swings faster than the biology, in both directions
bear_case.description: Tempus surged roughly 40% in a week on a data-platform announcement with no new clinical or regulatory event; Recursion rebounded 8-9% across two separate days on early, uncontrolled trial interest rather than results. Real moves, thin catalysts — proof this tier can re-rate sharply on narrative alone, which cuts both ways in a portfolio.

bear_case.title: A fund's own AUM can shrink even while its price rallies
bear_case.description: ARKG closed at a fresh 52-week high this week, yet its AUM fell from $2.00B to $1.93B over the same two weeks — consistent with investors redeeming into strength rather than new money arriving. A concentrated, actively managed fund can lose assets during its best stretch, not just its worst.

bear_case.title: Funding is recovering but selectively, and 2026's M&A pace is itself a valuation risk
bear_case.description: Average biotech deal size is up 44% y/y to $527M as pharma races to refill a patent-cliff hole worth over $300B in branded revenue this decade (only 4% of global drug sales will remain under patent by 2030, down from 12% in 2022) — but Q1 biopharma VC funding of $5.2B tilted heavily toward later, de-risked rounds with earn-the-back-end milestone structures, not early platform bets. A hot-M&A, friendlier-FDA rally can compress forward returns for anyone buying the rally rather than the underlying science.

Litigation still runs in both directions in diagnostics, unresolved as of this week.
